hook: If you care deeply about the people you talk to but somehow they still don't walk away feeling it — this is the exact reason why.
topic: Why caring doesn't automatically translate into people feeling cared for
body:
**If you genuinely care about the people you talk to — but they don't seem to walk away feeling that — it's not because you care less than you think.**

It's because caring and making someone feel cared for are two completely different skills.

Most people, when they care about someone in a conversation, show it by sharing. By relating. By saying "I know exactly what you mean — the same thing happened to me."

And what the other person feels in that moment isn't understood. They feel redirected.

The most connecting thing you can do in a conversation isn't to match their experience. It's to stay in theirs a little longer before you move to yours.

One extra question. Not an informational one — not "when did that happen?" But an invitational one. "What was that like for you?"

That question does something specific. It says: I'm not in a hurry to respond. I'm interested in the part of this you haven't said yet.

That is what people feel as warmth. Not your intention to connect — your willingness to wait.

Full listening framework is in my bio.
